subject: physics

concepts.title: Electrification and Polarity of Charge
concepts.definition: Bodies develop electric charge through friction or contact with another material, exhibiting either positive or negative polarity.
concepts.key_idea: Frictional contact transfers light charged particles without creating net new charge.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics explain electrification by friction
describe how glass rod gets positively charged when rubbed with silk
what is polarity of electric charge acquired during contact
why do unlike charges attract and like charges repel
explain how gold-leaf electroscope detects electric charge

solution_steps.explain: electrons shift from glass to silk during friction causing positive charge on glass
body losing electrons becomes positively charged while body gaining electrons becomes negatively charged
unlike charges attract and like charges repel confirming polarity assignment

concepts.title: Conductors and Insulators
concepts.definition: Conductors permit free flow of electric charges across their volume, whereas insulators restrict charge movement to localized regions.
concepts.key_idea: Mobile charges in conductors distribute over the entire surface while remaining fixed on insulators.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics distinguish conductors from insulators
explain why metal spoon held in hand cannot be charged by rubbing
how does excess charge distribute on a conducting surface
what is the role of grounding in discharging conductors
why does plastic comb get electrified when combed through dry hair

solution_steps.explain: free electrons in metals allow charge to leak through human body to earth

solution_steps.action: classify material as conductor or insulator
solution_steps.explain: conductors have free charge carriers that redistribute across the surface while insulators localize charge at the point of contact
insulators retain transferred charge because electrons cannot flow freely whereas conductors discharge through any grounding path

concepts.title: Additivity of Electric Charges
concepts.definition: The total charge of a discrete multi-particle system is equal to the scalar sum of individual charges taking algebraic signs into account.
concepts.key_idea: Electric charge is a scalar quantity requiring proper positive and negative signs during summation.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics state additivity of electric charge
calculate net charge of system containing discrete point charges
find total charge for system of point charges with positive and negative signs
how do charges add algebraically in a isolated system
determine combined charge when multiple point charges are brought together

solution_steps.explain: add magnitudes taking positive and negative signs into account
positive charges contribute positively and negative charges contribute negatively to the total
the scalar sum with proper signs gives the total charge of the system

concepts.title: Conservation of Electric Charge
concepts.definition: The total algebraic sum of charges in an isolated system remains constant regardless of internal processes or particle transformations.
concepts.key_idea: Net electric charge cannot be created or destroyed in any physical process.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics state law of conservation of charge
explain charge conservation during decay of neutron into proton and electron
verify charge conservation during frictional electrification
why is total charge of an isolated system invariant
describe pair production in relation to charge conservation

solution_steps.action: verify initial and final net charges
solution_steps.explain: net charge before reaction equals net charge after reaction

solution_steps.action: list all charges before the process
solution_steps.explain: sum the algebraic charge of every particle in the isolated system at the start

solution_steps.action: confirm equality of initial and final totals
solution_steps.explain: charge conservation requires the total algebraic charge to remain unchanged through any internal process

concepts.title: Quantisation of Charge Accumulation
concepts.definition: Electric charge carried by any physical object occurs in integral multiples of the fundamental unit of electronic charge e.
concepts.key_idea: Microscopic electric charge exists in discrete quanta equal to elementary charge e.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics find time required to collect target charge given electron transfer rate
calculate time taken to accumulate charge C when electrons leave body per second
determine duration needed to accumulate target charge from rate of electron loss
compute time to accumulate target electric charge
evaluate time required for electron flow rate to build target charge

solution_steps.explain: multiply electron emission rate by electronic charge e
divide target total charge by charge accumulated per second

solution_steps.action: verify time result is positive and finite
solution_steps.explain: a valid accumulation time must be a positive real number consistent with the electron transfer rate

concepts.title: Coulomb's Law Force
concepts.definition: Electrostatic interaction force between two stationary point charges is proportional to product of charge magnitudes and inversely proportional to square of separation distance.
concepts.key_idea: Point charges exert equal and opposite central electrostatic forces obeying inverse square dependence.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics calculate Coulomb force between two point charges
find electrostatic force between charges separated by distance r
determine force of interaction between two point charges in free space
compute magnitude of electric force using Coulomb law
evaluate repulsive or attractive Coulomb force for given pair of charges

solution_steps.action: multiply magnitudes of the two charges
solution_steps.explain: compute product of charge values q1 and q2
multiply separation distance r by itself
multiply Coulomb constant k by charge product and divide by distance squared

concepts.title: Ratio of Electrostatic to Gravitational Force
concepts.definition: The relative strength comparison between electrostatic attraction or repulsion and universal gravitational attraction for a pair of charged particles.
concepts.key_idea: Electrostatic forces dominate gravitational forces by many orders of magnitude for subatomic particles.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics compute ratio of electric force to gravitational force for two particles
calculate ratio of electrostatic force to gravitational attraction between electron and proton
find relative strength of Coulomb force compared to gravitational force for two protons
determine ratio of electrostatic interaction force to gravitational interaction force
evaluate how many times electric force exceeds gravitational force between two masses

solution_steps.explain: multiply electrostatic constant k by charge magnitudes q1 and q2
multiply gravitational constant G by particle masses m1 and m2

solution_steps.action: compute ratio of electrostatic force to gravitational force
solution_steps.explain: divide electric force numerator product by gravitational denominator product

concepts.title: Superposition Principle for Electrostatic Forces
concepts.definition: The resultant electrostatic force on a target charge within a multi-charge system equals vector sum of forces exerted individually by all other charges.
concepts.key_idea: Individual pairwise Coulomb forces remain unaffected by the presence of surrounding charges.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics state principle of superposition for electric forces
find net electrostatic force on a charge at centroid of equilateral triangle
calculate total force on a charge due to system of multiple charges
how to perform vector addition of Coulomb forces for multiple point charges
explain why pairwise forces are unaltered by surrounding charges

solution_steps.explain: sum individual Coulomb force vectors acting on target charge
calculate the Coulomb force between the target charge and every other charge using the inverse square law
decompose each force vector into components then sum component-wise to obtain the net force vector

concepts.title: Electric Field of a Point Charge
concepts.definition: The electric field intensity at a spatial location equals force experienced per unit positive test charge placed at that location.
concepts.key_idea: Source charge produces radial electric field decreasing inversely with square of distance.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics calculate electric field magnitude at distance r from point charge
find electric field intensity generated by point charge q at distance r
determine magnitude of electric field produced by source charge
compute electric field strength at distance r from charge
evaluate electrostatic field magnitude due to single point charge

solution_steps.explain: multiply distance r by itself
multiply Coulomb constant k by charge q and divide by distance squared
field points radially outward for positive q and inward for negative q with magnitude decreasing as inverse square of distance

concepts.title: Particle Acceleration in Uniform Electric Field
concepts.definition: Acceleration undergone by a charged particle moving through an electric field equals ratio of electric force to particle mass.
concepts.key_idea: Electric force accelerates charged particles proportional to field magnitude and inversely to mass.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics calculate acceleration of charged particle in uniform electric field
find acceleration experienced by electron or proton in field intensity E
determine acceleration of particle with charge e and mass m in field E
compute acceleration of electron in uniform electric field
evaluate rate of velocity change for proton in electric field

solution_steps.explain: multiply charge magnitude e by electric field strength E
divide electric force by particle mass m
acceleration is parallel to field for positive charge and antiparallel for negative charge with magnitude inversely proportional to mass

concepts.title: Properties of Electric Field Lines
concepts.definition: Imaginary continuous curves visualising electric field orientation whose tangent at any point gives net field direction.
concepts.key_idea: Field lines originate on positive charges, terminate on negative charges, and never intersect.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics list key properties of electric field lines
why can two electric field lines never cross each other
explain why electrostatic field lines do not form closed loops
how does relative density of field lines indicate field strength
draw electric field lines for pair of equal positive charges

solution_steps.explain: intersection implies two field directions at one point which is physically impossible

solution_steps.action: verify origin and termination of field lines
solution_steps.explain: field lines start on positive charges and end on negative charges or extend to infinity never forming closed loops in electrostatics

solution_steps.action: confirm line density indicates field strength
solution_steps.explain: regions where field lines are closely packed correspond to stronger electric field and sparse regions correspond to weaker field

concepts.title: Electric Flux through a Surface
concepts.definition: Measure of total electric field lines passing normally through a given area element.
concepts.key_idea: Flux depends on electric field strength, area magnitude, and inclination angle with area normal.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics calculate electric flux through planar area
find electric flux passing through surface area A tilted at angle theta
determine flux of electric field vector across planar surface
compute electric flux when electric field makes angle theta with normal
evaluate total flux through flat face of area A in uniform electric field E

solution_steps.explain: multiply electric field magnitude E by area A and cosine of angle theta

solution_steps.action: identify the angle between field and area normal
solution_steps.explain: theta is measured between the electric field vector and the outward normal to the surface area element
positive flux means field exits the surface while zero flux occurs when field is parallel to the surface plane

concepts.title: Electric Field on Dipole Axis
concepts.definition: Electric field produced by a pair of equal and opposite charges at a point lying along the line joining them.
concepts.key_idea: Axial dipole field decreases inversely with cube of distance and points along dipole moment.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics calculate axial electric field of dipole at distance r
find electric field intensity on axis of electric dipole at distance r
determine electric field magnitude at point on dipole axis far from centre
compute axial field produced by dipole moment p at distance r
evaluate axial field strength of short electric dipole

solution_steps.explain: multiply 2 by Coulomb constant k and dipole moment p
raise axial distance r to power 3
divide numerator product by distance cubed

concepts.title: Electric Field on Dipole Equatorial Line
concepts.definition: Electric field produced by an electric dipole at a point on its perpendicular bisector plane.
concepts.key_idea: Equatorial dipole field is half the axial field magnitude at same distance and points antiparallel to dipole moment.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics calculate equatorial electric field of dipole at distance r
find electric field intensity on normal bisector of dipole at distance r
determine electric field at broadside-on position of electric dipole
compute equatorial field produced by dipole moment p at distance r
evaluate field magnitude on equatorial plane of short electric dipole

solution_steps.explain: raise equatorial distance r to power 3
multiply Coulomb constant k by dipole moment p and divide by distance cubed

solution_steps.action: verify field direction relative to dipole moment
solution_steps.explain: equatorial field points antiparallel to the dipole moment and is half the axial field magnitude at the same distance

concepts.title: Torque on Electric Dipole in Uniform Field
concepts.definition: Rotational couple experienced by an electric dipole in a uniform external field seeking to align dipole moment with field direction.
concepts.key_idea: Uniform electric field exerts zero net force but non-zero torque on an inclined electric dipole.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics derive torque on electric dipole in uniform field
what is net translational force on dipole placed in uniform electric field
find orientation of dipole for maximum torque in electric field
explain how non-uniform field exerts net attraction on polarized paper
describe behavior of electric dipole in uniform external field

solution_steps.explain: equal opposite forces qE and -qE create net torque pE sin(theta) while net force is zero

solution_steps.action: determine torque magnitude from dipole moment and field
solution_steps.explain: torque equals dipole moment p times electric field E times sine of the angle between them

solution_steps.action: verify equilibrium orientation of the dipole
solution_steps.explain: torque is maximum when dipole is perpendicular to field and zero when dipole aligns parallel or antiparallel to the field

concepts.title: Enclosed Charge from Gauss's Law
concepts.definition: Fundamental theorem stating net electric flux through any closed Gaussian surface equals enclosed charge divided by permittivity of free space.
concepts.key_idea: Total electric flux across closed boundary depends strictly on total interior charge.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics calculate enclosed charge from electric flux using Gauss law
find total charge inside closed Gaussian surface given net electric flux
determine charge contained within cylinder or cube from total outward flux
compute net interior charge using Gauss law flux relation
evaluate charge enclosed by surface given total electric flux

solution_steps.explain: multiply net electric flux by vacuum permittivity constant epsilon_0
select a closed surface enclosing the charge distribution so that flux is calculable using symmetry
the computed enclosed charge must match the algebraic sum of all charges inside the closed Gaussian surface

concepts.title: Electric Field of Charged Infinite Wire
concepts.definition: Radial electric field generated by an infinitely long straight conductor bearing uniform linear charge density.
concepts.key_idea: Line charge creates cylindrical radial electric field decreasing inversely with radial distance r.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics calculate electric field at distance r from infinite long charged wire
find electric field intensity due to long straight wire with linear charge density
determine field produced by infinite line charge at distance r
compute radial electric field around long uniformly charged wire
evaluate electric field strength created by wire of linear charge density lambda

solution_steps.explain: multiply 2, pi, vacuum permittivity epsilon_0, and radial distance r
divide linear charge density lambda_charge by denominator factor

solution_steps.action: verify field direction and distance dependence
solution_steps.explain: field points radially outward for positive line charge and decreases inversely with perpendicular distance r from the wire

concepts.title: Electric Field of Infinite Charged Sheet
concepts.definition: Uniform electric field produced normal to an infinite flat plane carrying uniform surface charge density.
concepts.key_idea: Infinite charged sheet produces uniform electric field independent of distance from plane.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics calculate electric field near infinite uniformly charged plane sheet
find electric field strength due to infinite planar surface charge density
determine electric field intensity produced by large flat charged sheet
compute field near infinite charged plate using surface charge density sigma
evaluate uniform electric field created by planar surface charge

solution_steps.explain: divide surface charge density sigma by twice the permittivity of free space epsilon_0

solution_steps.action: identify field direction relative to the sheet
solution_steps.explain: field is perpendicular to the sheet pointing away for positive sigma and toward the sheet for negative sigma

solution_steps.action: verify field is uniform and independent of distance
solution_steps.explain: the infinite sheet produces a constant magnitude field on both sides that does not vary with distance from the plane

concepts.title: Electric Field of Thin Spherical Shell
concepts.definition: Electric field created by uniformly charged spherical shell, behaving as point charge externally and vanishing internally.
concepts.key_idea: Inside a uniformly charged hollow spherical shell, electrostatic field vanishes everywhere.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Physics electrostatics state electric field inside uniformly charged thin spherical shell
derive electric field outside charged spherical shell using Gauss law
how does electric field vary with distance for thin charged spherical shell
explain why electrostatic field inside hollow conductor is zero
apply Gauss law to determine field inside and outside spherical shell

solution_steps.explain: Gaussian surface inside encloses zero charge hence electric field equals zero

solution_steps.action: apply Gauss law outside the shell
solution_steps.explain: for a Gaussian surface outside the shell the enclosed charge equals total shell charge giving field identical to a point charge at the centre

solution_steps.action: verify field discontinuity at the shell surface
solution_steps.explain: field jumps from zero inside to k*q/R^2 just outside confirming charge resides on the surface of the conductor

concepts.title: Quantization of Electric Charge
concepts.definition: The total electric charge on any macroscopic or microscopic entity is an integer scalar multiple of the elementary unit charge.
concepts.key_idea: Net electric charge comes in discrete integral bundles equal to the fundamental electronic charge.
question_patterns: calculate the number of electrons transferred to produce charge {q}
find the total charge when {n} electrons are transferred
determine the total electric charge corresponding to {n} excess electrons
what is the magnitude of net charge given {n} electronic charges
evaluate the number of excess electrons on a body with total charge {q}

solution_steps.action: divide total charge by unit electronic charge
solution_steps.explain: quantization relates total charge q to electron count n via q = n * e_charge
charge quantization requires the number of elementary charges to be a whole number with no fractional remainder
a positive n indicates electron deficit or positive charge while a negative n indicates electron excess or negative charge

concepts.title: Coulomb's Law of Electrostatic Force
concepts.definition: The magnitude of interaction force between two stationary point charges is directly proportional to their product and inversely proportional to the square of their distance.
concepts.key_idea: Electrostatic interaction obeys an inverse-square distance dependence along the central line connecting charges.
question_patterns: find the electrostatic force between two point charges {q1} and {q2} separated by distance {r}
calculate the magnitude of electrostatic repulsion between charges {q1} and {q2} at distance {r}
determine the force acting between point charges {q1} and {q2} placed {r} meters apart
what is the mutual electrostatic force between charges {q1} and {q2} separated by {r}
evaluate the magnitude of electric force between two charges {q1} and {q2} at separation {r}

solution_steps.explain: multiply the magnitude of both interacting charges
coulomb force depends on inverse square of separation distance
multiply electrostatic constant k with charge product and divide by squared distance

concepts.title: Torque on an Electric Dipole in Uniform Field
concepts.definition: A pair of equal and opposite charges separated by a fixed distance experiences a net turning moment when oriented at an angle in a uniform electric field.
concepts.key_idea: Uniform external electric field produces zero net translational force but a restoring rotational torque on an electric dipole.
question_patterns: calculate the torque on an electric dipole with moment {p} placed in electric field {E} at orientation sine {sin_theta}
find the magnitude of torque acting on dipole {p} in external electric field {E} with angle sine {sin_theta}
determine the turning moment experienced by dipole {p} in electric field {E} where sine of angle is {sin_theta}

evaluate the magnitude of rotational torque on dipole {p} in field {E} with sine angle {sin_theta}

solution_steps.action: multiply dipole moment by electric field
solution_steps.explain: calculate maximum possible torque magnitude p times E
scale product by sine of orientation angle

solution_steps.action: verify torque direction and equilibrium condition
solution_steps.explain: torque acts to align the dipole moment with the field and vanishes when the dipole is parallel or antiparallel to the field

concepts.title: Electric Flux and Gauss's Law
concepts.definition: The total electric field flux passing through an enclosed Gaussian surface equals net enclosed charge divided by permittivity of free space.
concepts.key_idea: Net electric flux through any arbitrary closed boundary depends exclusively on the total net charge enclosed within.
question_patterns: calculate the net electric flux through a closed surface enclosing charge {q_enclosed}
find the electric flux exiting a closed volume containing charge {q_enclosed}
determine the electric flux through a surface enclosing net charge {q_enclosed}
what is the net outward electric flux from a region containing net charge {q_enclosed}
evaluate total electric flux across Gaussian surface enclosing total charge {q_enclosed}

solution_steps.action: divide enclosed charge by permittivity of free space
solution_steps.explain: apply Gauss's law formula phi = q_enclosed / epsilon_0
choose a closed surface that encloses the net charge so total outward flux depends only on interior charge

solution_steps.action: verify flux sign matches enclosed charge sign
solution_steps.explain: positive enclosed charge gives outward positive flux and negative enclosed charge gives inward negative flux

concepts.title: Electric Field of an Infinite Line Charge
concepts.definition: An infinitely extended straight line with uniform charge per unit length produces a radially directed electric field inversely proportional to distance.
concepts.key_idea: The electric field around an infinite linear charge distribution scales inversely with perpendicular distance.
question_patterns: calculate the electric field at distance {r} from an infinite line charge of density {lambda_val}

solution_steps.explain: compute factor 2 * k for simplified line charge formula

concepts.title: Electric Field of an Infinite Plane Sheet
concepts.definition: A flat infinite plane sheet with uniform surface charge distribution creates a uniform electric field independent of distance on either side.
concepts.key_idea: Electric field created by a uniformly charged infinite plane sheet is constant in magnitude throughout space.
question_patterns: calculate the electric field near an infinite sheet with surface charge density {sigma}

solution_steps.explain: calculate denominator 2 * epsilon_0

solution_steps.action: divide surface charge density by denominator
solution_steps.explain: calculate field E = sigma / (2 * epsilon_0)

solution_steps.action: verify field is uniform and direction is normal to sheet
solution_steps.explain: the infinite sheet produces a constant field on both sides pointing away for positive sigma and toward the sheet for negative sigma

concepts.title: Total Charge and Field of a Spherical Shell
concepts.definition: A thin uniformly charged spherical surface holds a total charge equal to surface density multiplied by spherical surface area.
concepts.key_idea: Total charge on a spherical conductor shell distributes uniformly across its exterior surface area.

questions: What is the force between two small charged spheres having charges of 2 x 10^-7 C and 3 x 10^-7 C placed 30 cm apart in air?

The electrostatic force on a small sphere of charge 0.4 uC due to another small sphere of charge -0.8 uC in air is 0.2 N. (a) What is the distance between the two spheres? (b) What is the force on the second sphere due to the first?
Check that the ratio k e^2 / (G me mp) is dimensionless. Look up a Table of Physical Constants and determine the value of this ratio. What does the ratio signify?
(a) Explain the meaning of the statement 'electric charge of a body is quantised'. (b) Why can one ignore quantisation of electric charge when dealing with macroscopic i.e., large scale charges?

When a glass rod is rubbed with a silk cloth, charges appear on both. A similar phenomenon is observed with many other pairs of bodies. Explain how this observation is consistent with the law of conservation of charge.

Four point charges qA = 2 uC, qB = -5 uC, qC = 2 uC, and qD = -5 uC are located at the corners of a square ABCD of side 10 cm. What is the force on a charge of 1 uC placed at the centre of the square?
(a) An electrostatic field line is a continuous curve. That is, a field line cannot have sudden breaks. Why not? (b) Explain why two field lines never cross each other at any point?

Two point charges qA = 3 uC and qB = -3 uC are located 20 cm apart in vacuum. (a) What is the electric field at the midpoint O of the line AB joining the two charges? (b) If a negative test charge of magnitude 1.5 x 10^-9 C is placed at this point, what is the force experienced by the test charge?

A system has two charges qA = 2.5 x 10^-7 C and qB = -2.5 x 10^-7 C located at points A: (0, 0, -15 cm) and B: (0, 0, +15 cm), respectively. What are the total charge and electric dipole moment of the system?

An electric dipole with dipole moment 4 x 10^-9 C m is aligned at 30 deg with the direction of a uniform electric field of magnitude 5 x 10^4 N/C. Calculate the magnitude of the torque acting on the dipole.

A polythene piece rubbed with wool is found to have a negative charge of 3 x 10^-7 C. (a) Estimate the number of electrons transferred (from which to which?) (b) Is there a transfer of mass from wool to polythene?

(a) Two insulated charged copper spheres A and B have their centres separated by a distance of 50 cm. What is the mutual force of electrostatic repulsion if the charge on each is 6.5 x 10^-7 C? The radii of A and B are negligible compared to the distance of separation. (b) What is the force of repulsion if each sphere is charged double the above amount, and the distance between them is halved?
Figure 1.30 shows tracks of three charged particles in a uniform electrostatic field. Give the signs of the three charges. Which particle has the highest charge to mass ratio?

Consider a uniform electric field E = 3 x 10^3 i N/C. (a) What is the flux of this field through a square of 10 cm on a side whose plane is parallel to the yz plane? (b) What is the flux through the same square if the normal to its plane makes a 60 deg angle with the x-axis?
What is the net flux of the uniform electric field of Exercise 1.14 through a cube of side 20 cm oriented so that its faces are parallel to the coordinate planes?

Careful measurement of the electric field at the surface of a black box indicates that the net outward flux through the surface of the box is 8.0 x 10^3 N m^2/C. (a) What is the net charge inside the box? (b) If the net outward flux through the surface of the box were zero, could you conclude that there were no charges inside the box? Why or Why not?
A point charge +10 uC is a distance 5 cm directly above the centre of a square of side 10 cm. What is the magnitude of the electric flux through the square?
A point charge of 2.0 uC is at the centre of a cubic Gaussian surface 9.0 cm on edge. What is the net electric flux through the surface?

A point charge causes an electric flux of -1.0 x 10^3 N m^2/C to pass through a spherical Gaussian surface of 10.0 cm radius centred on the charge. (a) If the radius of the Gaussian surface were doubled, how much flux would pass through the surface? (b) What is the value of the point charge?

A conducting sphere of radius 10 cm has an unknown charge. If the electric field 20 cm from the centre of the sphere is 1.5 x 10^3 N/C and points radially inward, what is the net charge on the sphere?

A uniformly charged conducting sphere of 2.4 m diameter has a surface charge density of 80.0 uC/m^2. (a) Find the charge on the sphere. (b) What is the total electric flux leaving the surface of the sphere?
An infinite line charge produces a field of 9 x 10^4 N/C at a distance of 2 cm. Calculate the linear charge density.

Two large, thin metal plates are parallel and close to each other. On their inner faces, the plates have surface charge densities of opposite signs and of magnitude 17.0 x 10^-22 C/m^2. What is E: (a) in the outer region of the first plate, (b) in the outer region of the second plate, and (c) between the plates?
